summary: For each successful call of estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, write the pallet width, height, and depth in metres on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped after deferred_source_indices. Width and height are the factory face that call already matches, params.pallet_width_m and params.pallet_height_m, and the search template stays that face. The face-centre position and yaw stay the pose, and pose.position.z stays the range of that centre in the RGB optical frame. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices stay the lists published_admission_split already writes. Depth is the length of this pallet behind that face, along the camera-facing normal, measured from this capture's returns before return, while samples.points_depth_frame, the oriented plane, and best_pose are still locals, and stored on the outcome so publish_pose copies the three scalars. Of the points sample_face_points already returned, project each with project_points_to_plane_2d, subtract best_pose.tx and best_pose.ty, and apply the inverse of the row map transform_points_2d uses, the same map at minus best_pose.theta_rad. Keep a point when those prototype coordinates lie inside the factory rectangle: absolute x at most half of pallet_width_m and absolute y at most half of pallet_height_m, closed on the boundary. A load above that face, the floor below it, and a return beside the pallet fall outside that rectangle. The contribution is the negation of the signed point_to_plane_distance, the length behind the face; orient_normal_toward_camera has already made the far side negative. Sort the kept contributions. Take the one closest to zero, the return nearest this face plane, and grow a window while each step to the next kept contribution is at most pallet_height_m, the face height this match already uses. A later surface begins only after a larger step, so it stays outside the window. depth_m is the greatest contribution in that window. This pass does not draw from the node rng. No second length is substituted, and no flag is written. A failed estimate still publishes no PalletPoseStamped, and the failure diagnostic stays the admission lists it already carries. The two early returns in on_pair stay silent. Stage 2 still runs once, on the one candidate the admission split already admits. The rich message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the sizes belong to this capture while the scene can still change. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is that width and height are the factory face this match already used, and that depth is the far side of the returns inside that face which stay within one face-height step of the face plane.
hypothesis: PalletPoseStamped already carries this capture's face centre, yaw, and admission split, while the factory face this match uses and the returns inside that face stay inside estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2. Copying that face onto the pose result, and the far side of the returns that stay attached to the face plane, gives the handling process the width, height, and depth of the pallet it is about to approach.
